chapterBreakdown.gentle:
Once the remedy path is visible, the book can ask a harder question. The chapter turns to optimal noise and asks whether zero noise is always the right target.

That matters because reducing noise is not the same thing as proving that zero noise is always the right goal. The chapter asks where limits and tradeoffs begin.

This is where the chapter becomes more cautious. Lower noise can be valuable, but pushing reduction further can raise questions about realism or desirability.

The chapter keeps one useful limit visible. Raising this question does not mean the book now celebrates noise. It means the ambition of reduction has to be examined rather than assumed.

chapterBreakdown.direct:
The chapter asks about the right target for noise reduction. It argues that lower noise can be valuable without making zero noise the automatic goal.

That matters because remedy design naturally raises a harder question: how far should reduction be pushed before other concerns begin to matter?

This is the distinction it has to protect. The chapter is not abandoning reduction. It is questioning whether maximum tightening is always realistic or desirable.

The limit stays visible. Optimal noise is not a slogan for loving noise. It is a way of asking whether the best target may stop short of total elimination.

That prepares the next step. Once the target question is in view, the book can make the tradeoffs more concrete in the costs of noise reduction.
chapterBreakdown.competitive:
The chapter looks at the zero-noise throne and asks whether the room should always kneel to it.

That matters because less wobble can be good while still leaving the room with a harder ambition question about how far to keep squeezing.

This is where the chapter tightens its edge. The book refuses to become team chaos, but it also refuses to treat maximum reduction as a sacred target.

The discipline stays narrow on purpose. No optimization formula appears, and no one gets to act as if the chapter now loves noise for its own sake.

That is what sets up the next step. Once the throne is questioned, the book can show the concrete costs of pressing harder.
